facts.title: The Matenadaran
facts.text: Over 17,000 manuscripts, including about 10,000 in Armenian, and some 300,000 archival documents.

facts.title: Baghaberd burns
facts.text: More than 10,000 manuscripts evacuated from Tatev and nearby monasteries are destroyed in the fortress.

facts.title: Around 1,600 saved
facts.text: As the Armenian Genocide destroyed thousands of works, these manuscripts were saved from destruction.

facts.title: A basalt sanctuary
facts.text: Designed by Mark Grigoryan, it draws on the canons of medieval Armenian architecture.
The Echmiadzin Gospel: a carved ivory binding and precious 6th-century miniatures.

facts.title: 27.5 kg
facts.text: Copied between 1200 and 1202. By contrast, a liturgical calendar from 1434 weighs only 19 grams.

facts.title: Memory of the World
facts.text: The Matenadaran is inscribed on UNESCO's Memory of the World International Register.

ytTitle: Yerevan's Matenadaran, guardian of over 17,000 manuscripts
ytLead: On the heights of Yerevan, the Matenadaran holds over 17,000 manuscripts and some 300,000 archival documents. It has been on UNESCO's Memory of the World Register since 1997.
